items.title: USSF-627 mission
items.summary: SpaceX’s official USSF-627 page now confirms that Falcon 9 lifted off at 8:36 p.m. PT on 11 November 2026 from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. It says this was the seventh flight for the first-stage booster, which had previously launched NROL-179, SDA-T1TL-E, SDA-T1TL-A and three Starlink missions, and that after stage separation the booster landed on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: SpaceX Shares Slip Amid Upcoming Starship Test Flight Jitters - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Stock Market Today, Nov. 11: SpaceX Shares Slip Amid Upcoming Starship Test Flight Jitters Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool market wrap by Robert Izquierdo, dated 11 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, says SPCX closed at $139.75, down 2.33%, after early strength from the FCC accepting SpaceX’s application to acquire 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain Management faded as investors focused on Friday’s Starship Flight 15. He also flags the 8 December lock-up expiry and notes Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161%, including $7.6 billion from the AI business; volume was about 111 million shares, and the stock is down 13% since the 2026 IPO.

items.title: Nov. 13 Could Be a Huge Day for SpaceX Stock - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Nov. 13 Could Be a Huge Day for SpaceX Stock Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Johnny Rice, dated 11 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, treats Friday’s Starship Flight 15 as a major event for SPCX and quotes Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas calling a successful catch potentially “the biggest positive catalyst since the IPO.” SpaceX plans to catch both the Super Heavy booster and, for the first time, the Starship upper stage at Starbase after a window opening around 5:45 p.m. ET, then fly more than 22 hours, complete about 14 orbits and deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before a Saturday catch attempt; the author notes that none of the latest V3 boosters have been caught yet and that a miss could push the payoff further out.

items.title: Is SpaceX a Millionaire-Maker Stock? - The Motley Fool
items.snippet: Is SpaceX a Millionaire-Maker Stock? The Motley Fool
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Alex Carchidi, dated 11 Nov 2026, argues that buying SPCX today is unlikely to turn a typical retail stake into $1 million, because a $5,000 investment would need a 200x gain — implying a $364 trillion market cap if the share count does not grow, more than twice the $151.9 trillion global stock market at the end of 2025. He still sees strong near-term growth from Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion (up 161%), including $7.6 billion from Super Intelligence and Starlink’s 13.6 million consumer subscribers, but says not to buy the stock hoping it will make you a millionaire.

items.title: Is SpaceX Stock a Buy Right Now? - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Is SpaceX Stock a Buy Right Now? Yahoo Finance
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Robert Izquierdo, published 11 Nov 2026 and listed in this feed as Yahoo Finance, says the author would wait to buy SPCX despite already owning shares, after the stock fell below $121 following the midterms and later traded around $142 — still well below the June high of $225.64. He flags AI-regulation risk after Democrats took Congress and some Texas leaders, including Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, called for a halt on new data centers, plus the 8 December 180-day lock-up cliff, while citing Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion (up 161%) and Super Intelligence sales of $7.6 billion, more than half of the top line versus $813 million in 2025.

items.snippet: SpaceX Stock Shrugs Off AI Worries Ahead of Starship Launch Barron's

The article notes shares had closed above $159 after 21 Oct earnings (with $7.6 billion of AI revenue, more than $1 billion above estimates) before falling 12.5% in the two days after the 3 Nov elections to close below $124 last Thursday, and that the flight aims to catch both stages to support cheaper, higher-capacity launches for Starlink and in-space data centers.

items.title: SpaceX must face sex-bias claims after appeals court rejects arbitration request - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX must face sex-bias claims after appeals court rejects arbitration request Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters story, consistent with the Ninth Circuit’s 10 Nov 2026 opinion in Holland-Thielen v. SpaceX, says SpaceX must face sex-bias and related claims in court after the appeals court rejected its bid to force the case into arbitration. A 2–1 panel held that the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act applies; the eight former employees allege they were fired after circulating a letter about conduct they called sexual harassment. The ruling decides the forum, not the merits. Reuters.com itself was paywalled here (401).

items.title: Why SpaceX Could Be the Best Buy-and-Hold Stock of the Decade - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: Why SpaceX Could Be the Best Buy-and-Hold Stock of the Decade Yahoo Finance

It frames launch, Starlink broadband, and the AI business as the main engines of that decade-long case; it is an opinion piece, not a company forecast.

items.snippet: BT to hold off Starlink launch until Ukraine 'noise' dies down, CEO tells FT Reuters
items.summary: The Reuters headline, as carried in an Investing.com reprint of the same wire, is that BT will delay launching its Starlink service until public “noise” over Ukraine dies down, according to CEO Allison Kirkby speaking to the Financial Times. Open coverage of that interview says the product is ready and BT still expects to launch in coming months; the Reuters page itself returned 401 here.

items.snippet: Elon Musk Just Gave the Top End of His SpaceX Revenue Forecast About a 2% Chance. His Best Guess Sits at the Bottom End. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: This Yahoo Finance story (also run by The Motley Fool) says Musk told the Baron Investment Conference that year-end 2027 annual recurring revenue is “quite likely” to top $500 billion — his “best guess,” not a promise — and put roughly 2% odds on $1 trillion. It notes even the low end would be five times a $100 billion December 2026 pace he discussed, while the stock was then only a little above the $135 IPO price and about 38% below a $225.64 52-week high.

items.title: SpaceX plans $24 billion gas power plant, data center project in Texas - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX plans $24 billion gas power plant, data center project in Texas Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report, also carried on Investing.com, says SpaceX is planning a roughly $24 billion gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas, according to a public-hearing notice, and has applied for a property-tax abatement. The Starbase City Commission is slated to consider the abatement and a related economic-development agreement on 9 Dec 2026; Reuters.com itself returned 401 here, so this follows the open wire reprint and the public notice as quoted there.

items.title: SpaceX now fundamentally an "infrastructure company," senior official says - Ars Technica
items.snippet: SpaceX now fundamentally an "infrastructure company," senior official says Ars Technica
items.summary: Ars Technica quotes SpaceX vice president of launch Kiko Dontchev at the UP.Summit in Florida saying the company is “fundamentally an infrastructure company at this point,” not only a rocket firm, after the rise of Starlink and a push into data and AI. Dontchev also discussed Falcon 9’s path toward retirement as Starship takes over, according to the article.

items.title: SpaceX will launch epic double-catch Starship Flight 15 test mission on Nov. 13 - Space
items.snippet: SpaceX will launch epic double-catch Starship Flight 15 test mission on Nov. 13 Space
items.summary: Space.com reports that SpaceX is targeting Friday 13 Nov 2026 for Starship Flight 15, in a 75-minute window opening at 5:45 p.m. EST from Starbase, in the first attempt to catch both Super Heavy and Ship at the tower. The mission description quoted in the article also calls for deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites and a more than 22-hour flight of about 14 orbits at roughly 275 km, longer than Flight 14’s Pacific splashdown.

items.title: SpaceX's December Lockup Is Nearly the Biggest Share Unlock in IPO History. History Says This Is What Happens Next. - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX's December Lockup Is Nearly the Biggest Share Unlock in IPO History. History Says This Is What Happens Next. Yahoo Finance
items.summary: This Yahoo Finance syndication of a Motley Fool column says SpaceX listed with only about 5% of shares in the public float, which the author links to early volatility and a denied S&P 500 fast-track bid, and that another 17% becomes eligible to trade in December (the article cites Dec. 9), leaving mainly Musk’s summer-2027 lock-up still closed. It recalls that the 22 Oct unlock of 1.3 billion shares — described as the largest in history, more than $180 billion — was followed by a 9% one-day drop, contrasts that with an early-August unlock after which the stock later rallied about 32% for the month, and argues investors should not try to trade the December event.

An IR note the same day thanks Harrison, who had served since February 2015 and is President of Global Partnerships and Corporate Development at Google.

items.title: Russia using own version of Starlink for military comms over Ukraine, Kyiv says - Reuters
items.snippet: Russia using own version of Starlink for military comms over Ukraine, Kyiv says Reuters
items.summary: A Reuters report by Daniel Flynn, dated 6 Nov 2026, cites Ukraine’s military intelligence (GUR) as saying Russia is already using its new Rassvet satellite network — billed as a homegrown Starlink analogue — for military communications over Ukraine, with the aim of making strike drones more accurate and harder to jam. GUR says Russia launched 32 Rassvet satellites in March and July, that coverage over Ukraine is still intermittent when satellites pass overhead, and that further launches are planned by the end of 2026; the article also notes that SpaceX earlier this year disabled grey-market Starlink terminals Russian forces had been using, and that temporary Starshield speed limits imposed on Ukrainian forces last month have since been lifted.

items.title: Go For Orbit — first revenue Starship mission documentary / recap
items.summary: SpaceX released “Go For Orbit,” a recap of the first orbital Starship flight to carry advanced Starlink V3 satellites — the company’s first revenue-generating Starship mission. Official posts describe more than a dozen prior flight tests and years of development; the public page is a JavaScript experience and did not return a long-form transcript here.

items.title: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms - CNBC
items.snippet: Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX lose over $420 billion in combined market cap after midterms CNBC
items.summary: CNBC reports that Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Thursday after the midterms, taking combined market-cap losses since Tuesday’s close to more than $420 billion on concerns that Musk could face new probes and tighter regulation. The article says Musk was a major GOP donor (more than $470 million, per the Financial Times) even as most of the candidates he backed lost, and that his estimated wealth dropped to below $800 billion.

items.title: SpaceX Stock Had These 2 Positives Today. It’s Still Falling. - Barron's
items.snippet: SpaceX Stock Had These 2 Positives Today. It’s Still Falling. Barron's
items.summary: Barron’s reports that SPCX was still falling after the election and had slipped below its IPO price, even as the story’s metadata highlights a new Buy initiation from China Renaissance with a $194.20 price target. The full article was largely behind a redirect/paywall here, so this summary is limited to that opening and the visible description.

items.title: Why SpaceX Stock Is Still Going Down - The Motley Fool
items.snippet: Why SpaceX Stock Is Still Going Down The Motley Fool
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Rich Smith, dated 5 Nov 2026, says SPCX was down 7.5% as of 11:30 a.m. ET that day — a second straight decline, taking the stock back below its IPO price — as investors worried a Democratic midterm sweep could bring new AI and data-center rules. Citing Axios, Goldman Sachs and StreetInsider, he notes newly elected Democratic governors in the four biggest data-center states and talk of a lasting “sell-AI trade,” while arguing that tighter earthly permitting could actually favor SpaceX’s plans to put data centers in space; he remains wary, calling the stock unprofitable and cash-burning.

items.title: Why SpaceX Stock Is Down Today - The Motley Fool
items.snippet: Why SpaceX Stock Is Down Today The Motley Fool
items.summary: A Motley Fool column by Johnny Rice, dated 4 Nov 2026, says SPCX was down 5.3% as of 2:53 p.m. ET that Wednesday, even as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were up 1.7%, after Democrats swept midterms that Elon Musk had spent heavily to influence, including $224 million in Texas. He writes that a Democratic Congress could complicate a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger and add hurdles for AI and data-center plans, though a new multiyear Qualcomm deal to build the ground network for Starlink Mobile helped buffer the fall.

items.title: Qualcomm signs major 5G infrastructure deal with SpaceX for Starlink Mobile network - Reuters
items.snippet: Qualcomm signs major 5G infrastructure deal with SpaceX for Starlink Mobile network Reuters
items.summary: Reuters reported that Qualcomm signed a major 5G-infrastructure deal with SpaceX for the Starlink Mobile network; Reuters.com itself returned 401 here. Open coverage of the same announcement, including Qualcomm’s own release and CNBC, says Qualcomm will supply radio and baseband gear for a nationwide terrestrial 5G network that complements Starlink satellites, with deployment expected to start in 2027 and financial terms undisclosed.

items.title: SpaceX signs deal with Qualcomm to provide network technology for U.S. mobile service - CNBC
items.snippet: SpaceX signs deal with Qualcomm to provide network technology for U.S. mobile service CNBC
items.summary: CNBC says SpaceX struck a multiyear deal with Qualcomm to build base stations for Starlink Mobile, a planned U.S. cellular service meant to complement the satellite network, with a rollout targeted to begin next year. Financial terms were not disclosed; Qualcomm’s Durga Malladi called it a chance to advance 5G and eventually AI-native 6G, and CNBC notes Starlink already accounted for 36% of SpaceX revenue and 85% of operating profit in Q3.

items.title: SpaceX inks Qualcomm deal, putting Starlink closer to becoming the fourth major US wireless carrier - Yahoo Finance
items.snippet: SpaceX inks Qualcomm deal, putting Starlink closer to becoming the fourth major US wireless carrier Yahoo Finance
items.summary: Yahoo Finance describes the Qualcomm agreement as a step toward making Starlink a fourth major U.S. wireless carrier, pairing satellite coverage with a terrestrial 5G build. It frames the deal as part of SpaceX’s push to add spectrum and partners after its consumer mobile offering had been limited compared with the big phone carriers.

items.title: How to Invest In SpaceX (SPCX) — And How Not To - NerdWallet
items.snippet: How to Invest In SpaceX (SPCX) — And How Not To NerdWallet
items.summary: NerdWallet explains how a retail investor can buy SPCX now that SpaceX is public — and how someone who does not want the stock might still end up with exposure through funds — after the 12 Jun IPO at $135 that raised about $75 billion at a $1.75 trillion opening valuation. The guide recalls a first-day close a little above $160 and a brief spike above $225, followed by a bumpier trade often below the offer price; it is an explainer, not a recommendation.

items.title: SpaceX Just Delivered a Monster Quarter, but the Stock Is Still Down 38% From Its High. The Reasons Are Obvious. - Yahoo Finance

items.title: SpaceX in talks to buy Boost Mobile or use its network, Washington Post reports - Reuters
items.snippet: SpaceX in talks to buy Boost Mobile or use its network, Washington Post reports Reuters
items.summary: Reuters, citing the Washington Post, reports SpaceX has been in talks with EchoStar to buy Boost Mobile or gain access to the network Boost leases from AT&T and T-Mobile, as a possible shortcut into Starlink Mobile’s planned hybrid satellite-and-terrestrial U.S. wireless service. The report says Musk met EchoStar chairman Charlie Ergen last month, EchoStar had 7.38 million wireless subscribers at the end of the second quarter, any deal may need AT&T and T-Mobile consent because those leases may not transfer, and neither SpaceX nor EchoStar immediately commented.

items.summary: Google News labelled this only “SpaceX,” but the resolved URL is SpaceX’s official page for Starlink launch group 15-18. The page is a JavaScript shell; official posts and a Space.com report on the same mission say a Falcon 9 lifted 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg early on 31 Oct 2026, with the first stage landing on Of Course I Still Love You — the 118th Falcon 9 flight of the year, per Space.com.

items.title: SpaceX closes out October with 700th Falcon 9 launch to date - Spaceflight Now
items.snippet: SpaceX closes out October with 700th Falcon 9 launch to date Spaceflight Now
items.summary: Spaceflight Now reports that SpaceX closed out October with the 700th Falcon 9 launch, sending 27 Starlink satellites on the Starlink 15-18 mission from pad 4E at Vandenberg at 9:04 p.m. PDT on 30 Oct 2026. Booster B1093, on its 18th flight, landed about 8.5 minutes later on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific, the 231st landing on that vessel and the 675th Falcon booster landing to date; the article also notes SpaceX is winding down Falcon as it shifts focus to Starship.

items.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video) - Space
items.snippet: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video) Space
items.summary: Space.com reports that a Falcon 9 lifted 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg at 12:04 a.m. EDT on 31 Oct 2026 (late on 30 Oct local time), with booster B1093 making its 18th flight and landing on Of Course I Still Love You. The article calls it the 118th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, with the satellites joining a constellation already larger than 11,000 spacecraft.

items.title: 8-K — Item 8.01, Apollo GPU finance-lease commitment
items.summary: The 8-K says that on 24 Oct 2026 SpaceX signed a binding commitment for a master finance lease with an Apollo-managed lessor that will buy GPU pods and related equipment and lease them to SpaceX. The company expects about $40 billion of principal payments over roughly five-year tranche schedules, with closing targeted by year-end 2026 and deliveries in the first half of 2027; an IR release adds that the chips are next-generation NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs and that Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and KKR also committed.

items.title: S-8 — Cursor reoffer prospectus / S-8

The live EDGAR document could not be fetched here (403); contemporaneous descriptions of this filing put the registered reoffer amount at about 23.6 million Class A shares.

items.summary: SpaceX’s official third-quarter 2026 release reports revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% from $5.6 billion a year earlier, with net income of $4.4 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $8.8 billion. Super Intelligence revenue was $7.56 billion and Connectivity $5.25 billion, with 13.6 million Starlink consumer subscribers and $69 monthly ARPU; the company also completed its first revenue Starship mission, deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

items.title: Acquisition of Cursor (Anysphere) — 8-K
items.summary: An 8-K says SpaceX closed its acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor) on 14 Aug 2026, converting outstanding Cursor stock into 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares at an implied $60 billion equity value, plus 1,752,426 shares for vested RSUs before tax withholding. Unvested Cursor awards were assumed as about 29.1 million SpaceX RSUs and 44.4 million options, and the merger shares were issued in an unregistered Section 4(a)(2) transaction.

items.title: 8-K — Cursor (Anysphere) acquisition

Cursor stock converted into 389,289,254 SpaceX shares at an implied $60 billion equity value, with additional shares and assumed awards for Cursor RSUs and options.

items.title: SpaceX reports second quarter 2026 results
items.summary: SpaceX’s official second-quarter 2026 release reports revenue of $7.8 billion, up 92% from $4.1 billion, a net loss of $541 million, and Adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 billion. The letter highlights two Starship V3 flight tests in 90 days, $14.1 billion of contracted cloud-services sales, the announced $60 billion Cursor deal, 12.0 million Starlink consumer subscribers at $66 ARPU, $47.5 billion of backlog, and $100 billion of cash and marketable securities after the IPO.

items.summary: This 8-K furnishes SpaceX’s official second-quarter 2026 earnings release, the same document as the Q2 press item. The release reports $7.8 billion of revenue, a $541 million net loss, and $3.5 billion of Adjusted EBITDA.

items.title: SpaceX closes IPO, including full exercise of underwriters’ option
items.summary: SpaceX’s IR release says the IPO closed on 15 Jun 2026 with 638,888,888 Class A shares issued, including the full underwriters’ option for 83,333,333 extra shares, for about $85.7 billion of gross proceeds. Class A shares had begun trading on 12 Jun 2026 on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas under the ticker SPCX.
items.timeSource: datePublished on the official IR release page

items.title: SpaceX prices IPO at $135.00 per share
items.summary: SpaceX priced 555,555,555 Class A shares at $135.00 and granted the underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 83,333,333 more shares at the same price. The IR release said trading was expected to start on 12 Jun 2026 on Nasdaq Global Select and Nasdaq Texas under SPCX, with closing slated for 15 Jun 2026.
items.timeSource: datePublished on the official IR release page

items.title: SpaceX launches initial public offering roadshow
items.summary: SpaceX launched the IPO roadshow for 555,555,555 Class A shares, with an expected $135.00 offer price and the intended ticker SPCX on Nasdaq Global Select and Nasdaq Texas. The company also planned to grant underwriters a 30-day option for up to 83,333,333 additional shares.
